brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
Wenzhou Zaocha is a regional appellation for the early spring teas of Wenzhou in Zhejiang, picked from February. It gathers county brands such as Taishun Sanbeixiang, Yongjia Wuniuzao, Yueqing Yandang Maofeng and Cangnan Cuilong.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: Tea growing around Wenzhou is said to go back more than 1,600 years. The name became a geographical indication for agricultural products in May 2020, and the 2025 opening of the Zhejiang green tea harvest was held together with its own opening event in Cangnan on 14 February.
processing: Typical of green tea: picked, heated soon after picking to stop oxidation, then shaped and dried.
harvest_season: Picked from February, among the earliest spring teas in Zhejiang.
appearance_dry: Green leaf whose shape depends on the maker, as is usual for regional green teas.
appearance_wet: Usually soft green leaf that opens up in the water.
taste_profile: Known for tenderness, freshness and a sweet finish.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
